newsitem.title: USA: Gillette unit leaves computer battery business.
newsitem.headline: Gillette unit leaves computer battery business.

text.p: Duracell, a wholly-owned subsidiary of consumer products maker Gillette Co, said Tuesday that it is shutting down its rechargeable computer battery business, resulting in the reassignment of jobs with the possibility of job losses.
Duracell said in a statement that it will phase out the production of its DURACELL AND DURACELL PowerSmart brands of lithium ion and nickel-metal hydride rechargeable computer battery packs.
The battery maker said it will try to reassign the 236 workers in its Waterbury, Conn., facility that are affected by the decision to its other operations, where appropriate.
The company said it will offer comprehensive severance packages as well as career counseling and job search resources to those employees not reassigned.

Duracell said it is leaving the computer rechargeable business because an anticipated consumer market did not develop to its satisfaction. However, the company did say it will continue to make rechargeable batteries for telecommunications devices and camcorders, for which it believes a consumer retail market now exists.
The PowerSmart technology developed by Duracell will be kept, the company said. Duracell said it will continue to provide the technology as well as components to battery manufacturers.
